name: Scripted Montage Blueprint
additional_sources: transcripts/what not to do in editing.txt
use_when: A brief says montage without defining what the montage should accomplish.
The editor is choosing clips randomly from a large footage pool.
A section needs to compress information, emotion, or progression without becoming generic b-roll.
A documentary intro has powerful footage but lacks a clear story arc.
avoid_when: The montage is purely exploratory and the user explicitly wants discovery through cutting.
The sequence is already tightly scripted and needs only execution.
The available footage is unknown and must be inventoried before a reliable beat plan can be written.

timeline_pattern.assembly_rule: Every selected shot should satisfy a written beat or deliberately replace one.
timeline_pattern.grouping_rule: Related shots should be grouped into story beats instead of scattered randomly.
timeline_pattern.contrast_rule: Use repeating contrasts, such as wide-to-close pairs, when scale and human detail both matter.

motion.rule: Plan motion only after the montage intent is clear.
motion.use: Use motion to connect beats, reveal progression, or guide attention.
motion.avoid: Applying effects to compensate for an unclear montage purpose.

sound.rule: Write sound bites, music moments, ambience, and transition sounds into the beat plan.
sound.timing: Major audio cues should correspond to beat transitions or payoff moments.

captions.rule: Use captions to clarify beat meaning, not to explain a montage that lacks visual intent.
captions.avoid: Captioning every beat so heavily that the montage becomes a text dump.

color.rule: Use color consistency to make varied montage sources feel like one intentional section.
color.avoid: Letting mismatched source color make the montage feel accidental.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent the montage as an EDL or JSON list with beat labels before rendering. Use concat from beat-ordered selects rather than selecting clips ad hoc. Add beat labels such as subject-first, scale, human detail, danger, normal life, and consequence for documentary sequences.
implementation.remotion: Create a data array of montage beats and render each beat as a Sequence with explicit duration, source, caption, and audio cue.
implementation.blender: Use storyboard markers or strips named after beat purposes before animating transitions.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Write the montage beats in notes or timeline text placeholders, then replace each placeholder with a clip.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use sequence markers, labeled placeholders, or a selects stringout organized by beat instead of raw source order.

common_mistakes: Choosing clips because they look good rather than because they serve a beat.
Adding motion before the montage has a point.
Letting the montage repeat one idea without progression.
Scattering related shots instead of forming a clear beat.
Choosing B-roll as filler when the narration needs evidence or contrast.
qc: Can each montage shot be tied to a written beat?
Does the montage progress rather than merely decorate?
Are sound, caption, and motion choices attached to beat intent?
Would removing a shot weaken the beat plan?
Are related shots grouped into intentional beats?
Does the montage include contrast when the story needs scale and detail?
